checks.name: Authenticated seeded browser matrix
checks.scope_rationale: Scoped to public launch on 2026-07-28. The owner has walked the signed-in product in production — signup, login, Stripe trial, access, cancel, AI generation and lifecycle email — and it works (docs/evidence/2026-07-28-owner-production-walkthrough.md). Calling the core journey unproven after that would be the gate wrong in the cautious direction, which is still wrong. What the matrix adds over one person clicking the happy path is phone and keyboard operation, cross-account isolation driven in a real browser, and the failure paths (session expiry, provider timeout mid-generation, reload during export). A supervised cohort of invited accounts with the owner watching can absorb those; strangers arriving unannounced cannot. So it stays required for public_paid.
checks.note: Built by SC-V11-03 (desktop, phone and keyboard projects over seeded isolated data). NOT RUN: it needs a database that has opted in via backend/migrations/E2E_MARKER.sql. The runner exits non-zero with a BLOCKED message rather than skipping. See docs/RUNBOOK_AUTH_E2E.md.

blockers.severity_history: Downgraded from P0 on 2026-07-28. The P0 rested on the claim that the signed-in journey had never been executed at all. That was true of automated browser runs and false of the product: the owner has run signup, login, Stripe trial, access, cancel and generation against production. The remaining gap — phone, keyboard, cross-account isolation and failure paths — is a public-launch condition, not a capped-beta one.
blockers.title: The signed-in journey has never been executed in a browser at any commit
blockers.closure: The matrix now exists (SC-V11-03). Point it at a non-production Supabase project per docs/RUNBOOK_AUTH_E2E.md, run `npm run test:e2e:auth`, and record the result against the candidate SHA.

accepted_risk.rationale: Owner decision to open public signup without the automated signed-in matrix. The owner has walked signup, login, Stripe trial, access, cancel, generation and lifecycle email against production, so the happy path is proven by use rather than by suite. What stays unproven is phone layout, keyboard-only operation, cross-account isolation driven in a browser, and failure paths (session expiry, provider timeout mid-generation, reload during export). Mitigation: AI_GENERATION_PAUSED=1 kills generation, Stripe refunds are immediate, and the cohort is small enough early that reports arrive directly.

blockers.title: Landing hero text does not meet WCAG AA (4.70:1 at the top, 1.99:1 at the bottom of the text band)
blockers.closure: Accepted for the capped beta on 2026-07-28: the v11 fix (in-hero scrim plus opaque helper/proof surfaces) was reverted because it dulled the approved blue and read as glass cards. Open for public paid launch. Options that leave the blue alone are listed under UX-V11-CONTRAST in docs/UX_DEFECT_LEDGER_V11.md. Held by backend/tests/landing-contrast.test.js, which pins the measured ratios and fails if the hero gets worse.

accepted_risk.rationale: Owner decision after rejecting the v11 fix twice: the scrim dulled the approved brand blue and the surfaces read as glass cards. White hero text measures 4.70:1 at the top of the hero and 1.99:1 at the bottom of the text band against AA's 4.5:1, so the CTA note and proof strip are the least readable copy on the page. Accepted as a commercial and design call, not as a claim that it passes. Options that leave the blue untouched are recorded under UX-V11-CONTRAST.

blockers.closure: Execute docs/RUNBOOK_TRANSACTION_REHEARSAL.md and attach anonymized evidence.

accepted_risk.rationale: Owner has run a live trial start, granted access and cancellation against real Stripe, and production shows 0 webhook failures in 24h. Not rehearsed: the nine-transition matrix, and specifically a late payment_failed arriving AFTER a recovery, which is the ordering case the v10 SC-00 fix exists for. If that fix is wrong a paying customer loses access. Mitigation: entitlement is reconciled from Stripe as canonical, refunds are immediate, and the owner monitors webhook_failures_24h on /api/admin/readiness.

capped_beta.note: GO for a capped, supervised beta only — 15-25 invited accounts behind BETA_INVITE_CAP, with the owner watching, per docs/BETA_PLAN_V10.md. Computed by `npm run launch:gate`, not declared: every required check ran at candidate 1145bae, migrations are verified applied against production, production configuration was answered by /api/admin/readiness in production mode with 0 blockers, and the owner has walked the signed-in product end to end on live Stripe. This is NOT permission to open public signup. Two known gaps ride along deliberately: the authenticated browser matrix has never run (phone, keyboard, cross-account isolation, failure paths) and hero text does not meet WCAG AA. Both are accepted at this cohort size because a named owner is watching and the cap is hard; neither is acceptable for strangers.

public_paid.note: GO on ACCEPTED RISK, not on complete evidence. Every condition that was actually met is evidenced: migrations verified applied, production configuration answered by /api/admin/readiness in production mode with 0 blockers, unsubscribe suppression proven live in both directions, spend ceiling live at $15, and the full local check set green at the candidate. Three conditions were NOT met and were accepted by the owner on 2026-07-28, each with a named rationale in blockers[].accepted_risk: no automated signed-in browser matrix, hero text below WCAG AA, and no nine-transition live billing rehearsal. Each keeps its real status in this file — `skipped`, `open`, `not_run` — so this document still says what is true. Reversing any acceptance returns this verdict to NO-GO automatically.

how_to_create_a_new_candidate: 1. Land all intended work on the release branch. No feature work after this point.
2. Set candidate.sha to the exact frozen commit and candidate.state to "frozen".
3. Re-run every required check at that SHA and record status, observed_at_sha and an evidence reference for each.
4. Attach owner evidence references for the live items.
5. Run `npm run launch:gate`. It recomputes both verdicts; it cannot be argued with.
6. Run `npm run launch:render` to regenerate docs/LAUNCH_STATE.md.
Any commit after step 2 creates a NEW candidate: the SHA no longer matches HEAD, every check pinned to the old SHA stops counting, and the verdict returns to NO-GO.
